_comment: gp-ladder proves the STRUCTURE holds: dependencies point backwards, kinds are
valid, a garbage response yields an empty ladder. None of that says the ladder
is teachable. A perfectly-ordered path through the wrong six ideas passes every
What this measures is the failure that was actually reported: the ladder for
'The water cycle' opened on 'States of Water: Solid, Liquid, and Gas'. A
learner who does not yet know what water IS cannot be taught that it has three
states — the path started on its second rung with the first one missing, and
looked completely reasonable while doing it.
So each case names a topic and asks: does step 1 assume anything? Is the
sequence one a teacher would actually follow? The checks are deliberately
loose about WORDING and strict about ORDER — there are many good ways to name
the first step of the water cycle and only one place it can sit.
startsBefore = a concept that must NOT already be assumed by step 1
ordered      = pairs [earlier, later] that must appear in that order
firstKind    = what step 1 has to be classified as
thresholdNote: A ladder is a judgement call and reasonable curricula differ, so this is not held to 100%. But a foundation that is not first is not a matter of taste — it is a learner stuck on step one — and below 80% the generator is producing tables of contents again.

cases.name: The water cycle starts with water, not its states
cases.subject: Basic Science
cases.note: The reported failure, exactly. Step 1 must not already be about a stage of the cycle — those are what the topic is FOR, not where it begins.

cases.name: Fractions start with what a part of a whole is
cases.subject: Mathematics
cases.note: Equivalence before addition is not stylistic: you cannot add fractions without common denominators, and common denominators ARE equivalence.

cases.name: Photosynthesis starts with the plant, not the chemistry
cases.subject: Basic Science
cases.note: A JSS1 learner needs to know a leaf makes food before any of those words mean anything.

cases.name: Simple interest starts before the formula
cases.subject: Mathematics
cases.note: Opening on the formula is the single most common way this topic is taught badly — the symbols mean nothing without principal and rate first.

cases.name: Family types start with what a family is
cases.subject: Social Studies
cases.note: The battle that prompted all of this ran on Family and its six questions were six unrelated sub-labels. A ladder here should read as one idea opening out.

cases.name: A ladder ends by tying the topic together
cases.subject: Basic Science
cases.note: The last rung is where the parts become a whole. A ladder that ends on another mechanism has taught the pieces and never the topic.

cases.name: Every step names something specific
cases.subject: Mathematics
cases.note: "Introduction to Algebra" is a chapter heading, not a lesson. Filler titles are the tell that the model produced a table of contents rather than a path.

cases.name: Steps are lessons, not units
cases.subject: Basic Science
cases.note: Three steps is a summary and fifteen is a syllabus. Each rung has to be teachable in five to ten minutes, which is what makes the < > navigation usable at all.
